scope: Standing exterior at Tytuvėnai. The Renaissance three-aisled basilica has a round-ended east chancel, exposed red-brick side walls, pointed windows, a high tile roof, and twin Baroque plaster towers over a low west vestibule.
geometryBasis: The mapped feature is localized in the geographic reference frame. The heritage register corroborates the specific building.
sectionBasis: The Renaissance three-aisled basilica has a round-ended east chancel, exposed red-brick side walls, pointed windows, a high tile roof, and twin Baroque plaster towers over a low west vestibule.
limitations: Tower, steep roof and vestibule section heights are visual estimates. Fine cornices, ironwork and carved frontage details are simplified.
The west vestibule is documented in the register and photographed. Its small projection is estimated because it is merged with the mapped west wall.

sources.use: Written heritage register inventory and section descriptions.
sources.controls: Three-aisled church with exposed brick and Gothic openings to the sides, a pale Baroque west facade and twin stepped towers, high main gable roof, lower lean-to aisles and a curved eastern end.

sources.use: The pilgrimage centre documents restoration of the church facades after the 2012 fire. The selected 2008 images guide historic form. Use published restoration facts for current scope and record any finish estimates.
The independently listed courtyard gallery is a current conservation project.
